question: Which of the following methods involves coating steel and iron with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting?
solution: The correct answer is __**Galvanisation**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **Galvanisation** refers to the process of coating steel or iron with a layer of **zinc** to protect it from **corrosion and rusting**. • The zinc layer acts as a **barrier** that prevents moisture and oxygen from coming into contact with the underlying metal. • Even if the zinc coating is slightly damaged, it continues to protect the metal by acting as a **sacrificial anode**. Zinc oxidizes faster than steel or iron, thus preventing rust formation. • Galvanisation is widely used in industries such as **construction, automobile manufacturing, and infrastructure development** due to its ability to prolong the life of metal products. • Common examples include galvanized pipes, roofing sheets, and wire mesh used in fencing.
